gaps.sentence: You are ___ a big risk if you invest all your money in one company.
gaps.explanation: take a risk means to do something that might have a bad result.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: The scientists are ___ research into new forms of energy.
gaps.explanation: do research (into something) is the collocation; 'make research' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: It took him months to ___ the habit of biting his nails.
gaps.explanation: break a habit (or kick a habit) means to stop doing something you do regularly.

gaps.sentence: The company has ___ enormous losses this quarter.
gaps.explanation: 'Suffer losses' is the standard collocation for experiencing financial loss.

gaps.sentence: The ministry has ___ an inquiry into the collapse.
gaps.explanation: 'Order an inquiry' = officially commission a formal investigation.
